data.leadership_messages: 1. The contractor has established a clear integrated planning architecture with a well-defined scope, creating a strong foundation for the continued development of the IMS2. Tasks are actionable and organized. WP are clearly defined to capture scope for production and manufacturing. 3. The cross-function dependencies are well mapped with detailed giver/receivers. Formal IMS incorporation will be completed during IIR 3 & 4.
data.rationale: There is strong confidence that the contractor has matured their planning architecture during the IIR #2 review. The WBS is mature, the contractor is making good headway on the scope, deliverables, scheduling planning and IMS loading. While the groundwork is mature, the next step is aligning detailed tasks within the WP to meet major program milestones. Overall, the contractor is ready to continue planning and integration toward IIR 3.

areas.text: CWBS Dictionary is well defined for GDT SERD implementation to gain NSA certification to include LOE support, RFP reviews and submittals, BOEs coordination and submittal and technical evaluation reviews. WPs are sufficiently defined with clear task completion criteria, many of the WP are generic and tied to CDR. However, the detailed planning contains detailed exceptionable actions. The integration of the OBS and RAM establishes solid accountability and work responsibility. While a minor concern was noted, the WBS dictionary and PSOW RAM currently align with SOW 8 instead of the updated SOW Rev 9 paragraphs, this does not significantly detract from the overall maturity and readiness of the architecture.

The contractor has made positive progress to establish a solid alignment with the IMP and the high-level planning structure/task definitions are steadily maturing. The contractor demonstrated a logical planning hierarchy with WPs and planning products that were clearly defined and organized. This resulted in executable tasks being developed into detailed planning. Workflow, dependencies, handoff logic, planning constructs, duration and assumption basis and QBDs had not been implemented at this phase of IIR#2. This was not a factor in the confidence rating. However, they will be ready for review and assessed in IIR#3.

The contractor has provided a highly detailed planning approach and a robust element-to-element giver/receiver list that clearly defines execution dependencies. While the physical incorporation of these dependencies into the formal planning structure—alongside supplier relationships, handoffs, and cross-product organizational transitions—is currently ongoing, the underlying logic and definition are mature. The contractor has a clear, actionable roadmap to fully integrate these elements in IIR #3 and #4

data.integration: This element is responsible for highly complex and critical interfaces spanning the AVE missile, STT, and ground systems. During this phase, the assessment was strictly limited to evaluating the preliminary Giver/Receiver (G/R) list. While the existence of this preliminary list demonstrates initial progress, the formal execution elements, such as detailed interface identification, schedule alignment, roles and responsibilities/coordination, and integration risk analysis, were not evaluated and are deferred to IIR #3 and #4
